name: Mag ni Dal
subtitle: loose split yellow moong finished with a ghee and cumin tempering, the plainest weekday dal

ingredients.qty: 200g, rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.note: use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Rinse the moong dal in three changes of water. The starch you wash off is what makes an unrinsed dal taste cloudy.
Soak 20 minutes if you are cooking in an open pan; skip the soak in a pressure cooker.
Salt goes in after the dal is soft, not before. Early salt keeps split moong from breaking down.

steps.text: Put the rinsed dal, water and turmeric in a pressure cooker and cook 3 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. In an open pan, simmer 30-35 minutes topping up water.
Open up and whisk the dal briefly. It should be loose enough to pour, like thin cream. Add hot water if it has tightened.
steps.tip: Mag ni dal is meant to be thin. If a spoon stands up in it you have gone too far.

steps.text: Stir in salt, the grated ginger and the slit green chillies and simmer 5 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan until it shimmers, then add the cumin seeds and let them turn a shade darker and smell toasted.
Add the broken dried chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida and pull the pan off the heat after 5 seconds.
steps.tip: Five seconds. Asafoetida burns almost instantly and turns acrid.

steps.text: Pour the tempering into the dal (it should hiss) and clap the lid on for a minute to trap the aroma.
Stir in the lemon juice and cracked pepper off the heat.
steps.tip: Lemon after the heat is off. Boiled lemon juice goes bitter.

steps.text: Scatter with coriander and serve over plain rice with a spoon of extra ghee.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens considerably. Loosen with hot water when reheating and add a fresh squeeze of lemon; the tempering aroma does not survive a second day.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
